rule_text: Entities must maintain a minimum capital cushion threshold of 10.5% of total asset valuation at all times.
All financial records must be audited and submitted within 15 days of the quarter's end. Any internal executive loans must be explicitly disclosed.
The organization must maintain an independent internal risk management committee comprising at least three non-executive directors.
Financial institutions must hold a stock of unencumbered high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) that is at least equal to total net cash outflows over a 30-day stress period.
Insider trading controls must enforce trading blackout windows starting 14 calendar days prior to quarter-end until 48 hours following public earnings announcements.
Material cybersecurity incidents must be disclosed publicly in SEC filings within 4 business days of determining that the incident is material.
Entities must maintain confidential and anonymous channels for reporting financial misconduct and prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers.
All material off-balance sheet arrangements and transactions must be explicitly disclosed in the management's discussion and analysis (MD&A) section.
All books and accounting records of financial transactions must be retained in an accessible format for a minimum of 6 years from creation.
Entities must implement a clawback policy to recover incentive-based compensation from executive officers in the event of a material financial restatement.
All client medical and financial data must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or a higher cryptographic standard.
Client records must not be retained for longer than 7 years post-policy termination unless the account is actively under legal review.
In the event of a data breach compromising protected health information (PHI), affected individuals and the regulatory authority must be notified within 72 hours.
Access to PHI must be protected by unique user identifiers and automatic logoffs. Audit logs must capture all views
A written Business Associate Agreement (BAA) detailing data safety requirements must be signed prior to sharing any PHI with third-party vendors.
The organization must distribute a Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) to all clients at service initiation and supply it upon demand.
All workforce members must complete mandatory cybersecurity and HIPAA privacy awareness training annually
Comprehensive security risk analysis assessments must be conducted at least once every 12 months to identify and mitigate threat vectors.
All transmissions of PHI over public networks must be encrypted in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.3 or higher.
Facilities housing servers containing PHI must restrict entry using keycards or biometric locks and log all physical visitors.
Data subjects have the right to request the deletion of their personal data without undue delay when the data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected.
Organizations processing large scales of personal data must appoint a designated Data Protection Officer (DPO) whose contact details are publicly accessible.
Granular consent must be obtained for each distinct processing purpose. Users must be able to withdraw consent easily
column6: and consent records must be timestamped.

Personal data collection must be limited to what is strictly necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed.
Personal data transfers outside the European Economic Area (EEA) are permitted only to countries with adequacy decisions or using Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs).
A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) must be conducted for any high-risk data processing activities before such processing commences.
Personal data breaches must be reported to the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of the incident.
Data subjects must be provided a copy of all their processed personal data and description of processing free of charge within 30 days of request.
Organizations must implement technical and organizational measures by default during system design to protect data privacy.
Corporations must publish an annual, third-party verified report detailing their Scope 1 (direct) and Scope 2 (indirect energy) greenhouse gas emissions.
Annual on-site audits must be conducted for all Tier 1 suppliers to ensure adherence to fair labor practices and the prohibition of child or forced labor.
Entities must maintain a formal board diversity policy targeting a minimum of 30% diversity of board membership.
Entities must maintain a waste management plan detailing waste diversion targets and aiming for a minimum 80% recycling rate.
Entities must conduct annual
column6: independent equal pay audits to guarantee gender and ethnic pay equity across all job grades.

Entities operating facilities in high water-stress regions must implement a water stewardship plan to measure and reduce freshwater consumption.
All corporate manufacturing and fulfillment facilities must maintain ISO 45001 certification or equivalent occupational health and safety standards.
Entities must publish an annual
column6: comprehensive report detailing all direct and indirect political contributions and lobbying expenditures.

rule_text: Entities must establish a formal community investment program committing at least 1% of net profits annually to local development initiatives.
